Review: Two of my three kids recently moved up into booster seats. We were traveling and needed to rent car seats while we were traveling. These were great to fold up and put in their backpacks for carry-on forthe airplane. They did add weight to the backpack, But what we saved in space and cost it was worth it. Definitely recommend this product! We have also used it when we have friends come to visit, or pick a friend up to go on a weekend excursion. It saves so much time and transferring boosters! One last comment and then, I promise I'm done! We have friends that have the cushion travel seat. I have noticed that it does not keep the kids high enough where the shoulder strap doesn't bother them. It also seems like they do not grip on the seat as well as these do. Granted, our friends may not have had access to this product when they purchased theirs, And of course every family has their needs. For us, this was the perfect product! Review:
I was skeptical, not because of reviews, but how this would work in "real life" going through the airport security.
We just got back and this cart has proved it's worth 10x over. I did NOT want to be stuck at the rental car agency rummaging through cheap car seats as I have in the past. So here's what I did...
I ordered one cart and EASILY strapped in my Britax Marathon 70. Since my kids are happy to walk, they would not be riding in it, I took the other childs Marathon 70 and plopped it right onto the other seat. The side straps don't reach the cart but the top belt reaches and all just cinch that real tight and you now have both seats on 1 rack. It was so good we used it as a cart to pull around our carry on with no tipping or other problems.

Security was a breeze. We told the ticket counter we needed to gate check the seats which was fine (AirTran). When we got to security, I motioned right away to the TSA guy these were oversize and he took it through the door. On the way out the one guard asked I separate the seats (1 minute later, done), on the return they said it was fine as is. They took it aside, hand checked it while me and the family walked through. No problems.

At the gate, we went straight to the counter to get tags for the seats, and folded up the cart for overhead carry one - and that was that, next stop was dropping/picking up at end of the walkway. It may have helped we flew off peak times so we didn't encounter lines.

Review:
We bought a Radian RXT in 2018 for our second child and loved it. It is easily the most secure car seat I have ever strapped my kid into, and we have owned a lot of Graco and installed in several different models and types of car. Also the easiest install, I've fought for more than 30 minutes in my mom's Ford Explorer with Graco and wanted to set the car on fire afterward for her making me move it over in 105 degree Texas weather. It is heavy, but I install mine and won't move it for any force in heaven or hell unless I am flying, so its not like I do a daily ruck march with it.

Unfortunately, Diono is charging the same price they did for once a premium fabric car seat cover and giving you a crappy, thin car seat cover. Just feeling the difference between the two year models, you can tell they downgraded for the 3RXT severely since putting out the RXT. It has less padding, it is much thinner and I don't see how it isn't going to pill in the wash. My kid is going to destroy it.

I've included pics of old versus new for reference, but most of it is in the "feel".

I find this very disappointing, because you want a quality fabric in a "upper trim" series car seat that is supposed to last 10 years and costs $300. It's the same cheap, slick microfiber that I have on a couple of wal-mart $30 booster seats, or on universal car covers. I imagine it will turn green/gray in the sun just like those did. My Radian RXT is the same color it was when I bought it and even at two years older, looks better and its been washed a zillion times.

At first, I thought they sent me a car seat with the wrong cover, because it says "Radian R" and my RXT was embroidered on, not stamped on the fabric like this one. It also shows on the box as "Radian RXT", so I think my confusion is reasonable. Then I looked at the pictures on their website and Amazon. Nope. They are all universally the same crappy fabric across the entire Radian series.

Shame on you, Diono, car seats are expensive enough when you have to replace them constantly as you have kids, or have more than one so you aren't dealing with the logistics of switching cars with your spouse or parents just to get kids from point A to point B. And parents could easily save themselves $100 or $200 by buying something a little less "premium".

Removing a star for the cheapness, because seeing it there makes me wonder if they are as "premium and innovative" as Diono claims. Companies that do things well would do well to do it across the board, especially if they want repeat business. I came back because I loved the RTX so much. Not sure if I needed another one that I would come back for a "4RTX" or whatever comes next unless they go back to better covers.

For reference, these install amazingly well in Toyota Corolla, Sienna and Highlander and even the tiny Prius, but rear face in a Prius puts the front seat up too far for anyone over 5'6 to sit comfortably (basically every adult in our family). It will install in a Ford Explorer, but you will still be angry if its leather, cause they really didn't want anyone to get anywhere near their latch to actually use them and they are set too close together, so actually cranking down and getting the seat tight enough is a hassle, but easier than installing a Graco carrier or convertible car seat. Don't let an entertainment package on a Ford Explorer fool you, not a young family with car seats car. :p

Review:
We own two of these seats. One we purchased in December 2010, and the second we purchased on December 2011 (we have two kids, one year apart). The first one we absolutely loved and still love. The seat is great, sturdy, easily adjustable, heavy enough, and our son quit screaming in the car ever since he's been facing forward. If you have light-colored seats, just a note of warning, with kids things get dirty very quickly, and these seats don't help (I end up cleaning the seats after we take them out, as they get dirty really fast, but I'm sure this is the case for every car seat).

The second one we received in 2011... well, let's just start with my main complaint: locking that sucker in, it's as difficult as installing and reinstalling the seat, or performing brain surgery. The front button with the red in the middle: it was previously a push down mechanism and it locked well, and if pressed well, then it'll unlock - a system that works seemlessly and was easy on your fingers. On the newer version, it's not a push down, but you have to press the button (a much smaller button than the old one), which not only breaks your nails, but requires some muscle.

The design is different and not quite as good as the old one. Moreover, you bring the two belts together and clip them, then you insert the little handles into the center red button and let me tell you... on the newer design, that task is nearly impossible. To lock your child, especially a wiggly one, is a task that takes us at least 10 minutes each time. It just doesn't lock, and it only does when you're stubborn enough to spend the time and patience to lock it. The clips and handles and all of that good stuff is at least 40% smaller on the newer model than it was on the older one. There's a front cover at the croch area, and in the old one it stays in place, it's thick and comfortable. On the newer version, it's smaller, thinner, and what's more, it falls off every time - we removed it permanently. The cover kept covering the locking mechanism making it astronomically harder to lock the belts, than it already is without it.

When you want a car seat for a toddler, you need something that locks easily and fast (I'm good with unlocking being difficult). On the newer seats, unlocking it is easy, but locking your child into the seat is so hard and time consuming it makes me wonder... how many people would give it up. I know that I'm less open to making stops, so that I won't have to take him in and out of his seat - it's just so painful.

The seat itself is great, but if the company would replace those straps and locks for something more functional, it would be a great improvement. The only reason it actually got the 3 stars instead of 1, is because we still love the first seat we bought, we just hate the newer one.

Review:
So far we love the car seat. My daughter has been using it for about a week. This included one long trip to an out of town doctor. She enjoys being able to look around and see out the windows. Everything amazes her since she could see that well from her previous car seat.

My daughter is almost two and actually has long legs and she has plenty of leg room now (and we don't even have it set to have has much leg room as this car seat can give of course). In her old carseat she propped her legs up on the back of the seat.

The car seat sits very securely rearfacing. It doesn't seem unsturdy at all. I have Dodge Grand Caravan and it's in one of the middle seats. In a smaller vehicle I could see issues with this car seat not fitting, though. It fits snuggly in my van.

It can be an issue to get her to sit up straight to fasten her in, though and if she isn't sitting up straight then she has that issue of her chin being tucked into her chest that other people have complained about in reviews. She doesn't seem to mind it but I feel like it is safer for her to be sitting up straight when fastened in.

The only negative and the reason I am giving it four stars instead of five is because she can't sleep fall asleep easily in it. She DOES fall asleep and is able to sleep okay in it but it takes her a bit to figure out ways to sleep and she has to be extremely sleepy to do it. I do believe that this would be an issue with almost any up right car seat though. She was use to her reclining baby seat. So, this is just different.

Oh and it did take my husband a little while to install it but he was able to get it installed securely and without getting annoyed with it. So, it must not have been to bad.

My daughter is special needs and has a weak spine and weak muscles. She needs to rear face as long as possible as it will take her longer to get strength in her neck and spine. So, I chose this car seat for its ability to rear face to 50lbs. And for that I do love it.

Final consensus is that it's safe and my daughter likes it. So, while I wish she could sleep (and drink her bottle) easier in it overall it's very worth the money and we will likely be purchasing another one of these for our next baby.

If I could return it I would but the box got wet. Since transitioning to this seat we hate going anywhere because our son can not tolerate this carseat. On top of the crying baby that now cries nonstop, It is very hard to tighten and loosen the straps. I'm not a wimp but getting any movement when you pull the strap to tighten the baby's shoulder traps is almost impossible. I pretty much only travel with my husband now because I don't feel confident in being able to this seat on my own it is that difficult.. Loosening the straps is just as bad. Apparently this is the case with the seats with the feature that clicks so you know it is tight enough. I worry about getting him out quickly in an emergency. With the other seat it wouldn't have been a problem. As it stands, after owning this for around a month I still have the same difficulty using it. It has not gotten any easier.

The fact of the matter is we went from having a content 7 month old who was happy in his infant carseat (Chicco kefit 30) and actually enjoyed car rides despite it being too small and cutting into his shoulders at the highest setting, to a 7 month old that cries the entire time he is in the seat unless someone sits in the back and distracts him with food. I never get to sit in the front when we travel any more and I won't go any place with the baby on my own because the difficulty of use and the crying. We took the shoulder pads off and that helped some so he isn't crying like he is in pain constantly and we reclined it as far as it goes and that also improved it as far as it goes. Traveling has been a nightmare with this seat. We even tried swapping back to the other seat and he was fine for traveling in that, he is just too big for it so it is not safe.

I will be saving up to buy a different seat. I just feel I wasted my money on this. I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND IT TO ANYONE even if it is on sale. I got this for $190 on a lightening deal. I suspect it was a deal because of these issues.

Review:
This seat gave us 17 months of infrequent use before the Clicktight (CT) feature rendered the seat unusable. Because we don't have a dedicated vehicle and instead use car-and ride-sharing services, knowing we would be able to safely, correctly, and quickly install a seat with a standard seatbelt in any vehicle, anytime, anywhere was what sold us on the Marathon CT. We were willing to pay more for the CT feature and lug this beast of a seat into Ubers and Zipcars, through airports, and on planes because we believed its quality and supposed ease of use was worth the extra weight and hassle. We still stood behind this seat when its quirks started showing (the harness tension was always slightly uneven no matter how many times we reset it; the harness adjustment area became a repository for crumbs and curious fingers; the selected recline angle was deceiving and would usually decrease once the CT system was engaged; the lower harness straps sometimes left marks on my child's legs; and so on).

Unfortunately, the CT system proved to be the demise of this seat. More often than not, the CT dial would only partially engage when I pushed the panel down with my hands, especially when all slack was removed from the seatbelt as instructed. Instead of clicking shut, the panel would bounce off a taut belt. A gentle kneel was almost always needed to fully lock or disengage the CT panel. The seat also was difficult to rear-face in our preferred rear center position in certain vehicles, with multiple attempts needed to ensure a no-budge install.

While attempting to install the Marathon CT rear-facing in the rear center position in Toyota sedan last weekend, I encountered my typical issue of the panel not fully engaging when pushed down. I gently kneeled on it to click it shut and the dial became displaced under the panel, making it inoperable. Because we were away from home at a special event, I looked for other ways to install the seat without using CT and found that using LATCH on this seat is (1) absolutely horrendous and (2) impossible to achieve safely without having a functional CT panel, as the LATCH belt path runs under it. We were grateful to make it home safely by doing a makeshift LATCH installation in an outboard seat (kind of like how you attach a seat to the Britax wheeled travel cart, which incidentally ALSO broke the same day - so much for Britax quality!). The LATCH belt was very difficult to loosen and it took 15 minutes for my spouse and I to remove the seat from the car. Worst of all, the seat is no longer safe to use.

I have since looked for information in the installation manual as well as on Britax's site about whether kneeling on the CT panel during installation is acceptable and have found nothing discouraging or forbidding it. The seat is no longer under warranty, but I reported the issue to Britax and am awaiting a response. If anything, the CT malfunction has greatly diminished my once-high regard for Britax's safety and durability. I am very disappointed and am looking for a non-Britax replacement.

Review:
I was lucky enough to score this seat in the cyber Monday hidden deal, and since I am a CPST, I wanted one as a backup as well as for education. My 4 month old is currently using this seat installed with the seat belt in the middle of our "13 Ford Explorer.
Pros:
*Ease of installation. It wasn't the easiest I've ever done, and I made the mistake of expecting to be able to reach in through the belt path. You can't, instead you pull back the cover and reach in that way. But overall, I'd say this is a pretty easy installation. The recline adjustment is awesome. Follow the manual!
*It's a nicely compact seat that is also long-lasting, which is a fantastic combination.
*I love how organized it is designed and the very clear instructions and stickers on the seat. Chicco did a great job wording the manual and clearly marking the seat. I also love the little compartments for storage on the seat.
* Kudos of Chicco for listening to their customers and allowing the strap covers to be optional (go to their website for more information)

Cons:
*It's a big seat. While it is nicely compact front to back, it is still quite heavy and bulky. Loading a child in and out can be a challenge and it's more of a bucket-shaped seat, which some kids may not like. It is also moderately wide at the widest parts of the sides, so puzzling with other seats may be a challenge if you are lacking in space.
*The harness tends to be very hard to tighten. I'm not sure if that will improve once the strap covers are removed. The pads also get in the way of being able to do the pinch test, and practically choke my son once I finally wrestle the chest clip high enough (have almost hit him in the face several times trying to pull/push the clip up!).
*The adjustable headrest can be frustrating to use. It's clunky and takes some finesse to figure out how to press the stiff button and raise the headrest and then find the locked position.

Overall, this seat is worth some of the day to day annoyances, and I'm sure with extended use, things loosen up and it becomes easier to do the necessary adjustments. But for me personally, this will be our #2 seat, behind the Radian RXT. There's just no contest when it comes to getting the baby in the seat and buckled and adjusted with ease.

Review: My daughter is 5 1/2 and tall for her age at 48 inches and 47 lbs. She just outgrew her harness in her Recaro ProSport. Since the ProSport was recently recalled, I was informed that because of the recall we could no longer use the latch in booster mode. So I wanted to replace it with a safe booster seat that latched to the vehicle for safety and convenience. Who wants a 30 lb projectile in their car, not me!! I considered the Clek Oobr and Cybex Solution Q-Fix. The Oobr apparently has a short seat pan and is uncomfortable for a lot of kids, especially tall kids like my daughter. The Cybex looks like a great booster. However I was recommended this booster by a CPST and at more than half the price of the other boosters it was a great value. It also becomes a backless booster which the Cybex doesn't do. It is also rated a Best Bet booster by the IIHS. The other great features that only Britax has is the safeguard which keeps the lap belt in the proper position and the safe cell in the base which reduces the forward movement in your child in a collision. At first when I looked at the booster online I had 2 main concerns. Was it upright and flimsy? I can now say no to both of those concerns. This seat is so sturdy and well made. Very solid and substantial. The fabric is very nice looking and great quality, very thick. My daughter loves the pink and it looks great in our van. The bottom part of the booster where the child sits is very well padded and has a thick cushion. The booster back hinges slightly which allows you to get a great angle in your car. I have seen other reviewers think this is a defect but it is designed like that so you can get a great angle for different cars. This seat fits perfect in my Honda Odyssey 2nd row captain's chair. It is so easy to latch in, it takes about 1 minute. My daughter has a perfect seatbelt fit in this booster. The headrest is very easy and smooth to move up and down. I was very sad to have to move her out of a 5 point harness but seeing her so well secured and comfortable in this booster has put my mind at ease. I have come to love the quality and safety of Britax! My youngest is in a Britax Chaperone and my 3 year old is getting the Frontier 90 to replace his recalled ProSport. Britax has great customer service as well. My ONLY complaint with the seat so far is that it is made in China, I wish Britax would produce ALL of their seats in the USA. Bottom line if you are looking for a booster seat, get this one you will not regret it!

Review:
Since 2001 I've been hooked on Britax car seats. The quality and ease of use of their seats puts them above their competition. When I was presented with the opportunity to review the Britax Pavilion 70-G3 I jumped at the chance to see how it compared to the Britax Marathon 70-G3.

The first thing I noticed when I pulled this seat out of the box was it's weight. This seat isn't one that you're going to want to transfer from one car to the next on a regular basis and I certainly wouldn't want to have to lug this seat through an airport.

My initial impression of the seat is that it was the overprotective parent's dream come true. I'm all for a super safe car seat for my child but this seat almost feels like overkill. The wings that protect the child's head in the event of an accident also keep the child from being able to turn his or her head and look out the window or at a passenger riding next to them. It also makes loading a child into this seat in the rear facing position a bit difficult. My nineteen month old who is used to riding in a Marathon 70-G3 and a Roundabout 55 Classic is not thrilled with the seat. In the past I have not been a fan of the HUGS that are on the harness for the Marathon seats, and I expected the new Safe Cell HUGS to be even more of a pain with regards to loading and unloading my child but they're actually a great improvement on the old HUGS feature.

The harness for this seat deserves some attention in this review. For about five months I put off using and reviewing this seat because I had difficulty loosening the harness when I first took it out of the box. I've handled a lot of car seats in the eleven and a half years that I've had children and this was the first seat where I had a lot of difficulty loosening the harness enough to get my child in the seat. I was so irritated by the seat that I put it out and my garage for several months and figured one day when I had more time I'd play with the seat a little more. When I finally got back to the seat I figured out what I was doing wrong. I always pull on the harness at the shoulder/chest clip area to loosen the harness (the hang tag instructions for this seat suggest pulling on the chest clip). Because the HUGS are tethered to the car seat shell doing this means the harness can't be pulled from the top. I found that if you pull the harness from the lap area the straps loosen with no problem. So I absolutely understand the frustration that many other parents have had with the harness.

Tightening the harness is simple. Just pull the center strap on the front of the seat and it makes a loud click when the harness is within an acceptable range of tightness. I think it's a great feature that will help those parents who tend to leave the harness too loose learn how to properly secure their child.

Harness height adjustment on this seat is a snap compared to the seats where you need to rethread the harness. You simply have to squeeze and pull (or push) to adjust the height of the harness straps. The ease of use for this function is on par with the simple adjustment of the back on a Graco TurboBooster.

Just like the Marathon 70-G3 the versa tether on the Pavillion is energy absorbing and works to reduce forward movement and rotation in a crash. The seat also has the EZ-Buckle System which keeps the harness buckle in a forward position and keeps your child from sitting on the buckle. I can tell you that this feature is quite nice. I had been using a Roundabout 55 Classic with our nineteen month old and I can't tell you how often she ended up sitting on the buckle and freaking out while I try to pull it out from under her. The new design really works nicely to keep the buckle out of the way when loading the baby into the seat. The design reminds me of the harness buckle on our B-Agile stroller.

Installation of this seat was a snap. I installed it both rear and forward facing in my Toyota Sienna and it was easily and securely installed in both positions. The seat is on the larger side so it is possible that this seat may not fit well in smaller cars when used in the rear facing position, but I think it's a bit more compact than the Marathon 70-G3 and Roundabout 55 Classic. Using this seat rear facing I have noticed that my toddler has less leg room with the Pavillion than she has with both the Marathon 70-G3 and the Roundabout 55 Classic.

Overall, this is a great quality seat that will keep your little one safe, comfortable and secure for many years. If you can deal with the ease of use difficulties with loosening the harness and your child doesn't mind having his or her view obstructed by the wings around the head then this seat is a very safe option with will offer optimal protection for your child. In the eleven and a half years that I've been using Britax seats, I have found each of them to be worth the price. While the Pavillion is a good seat, I prefer the Marathon 70-G3 for ease of use.

Review:
I'm a car seat psycho (for safety) and I've tried multiples of every version of seat (infant, convertible, HBB...) to find the very best of the best. After 3 different HBBs, this Peg Flex is the holy grail. Here's why:

It doesn't have arm rests so your kid can actually do the buckle unassisted. This is huge because you go from a kid that can do their convertible seat straps to a kid that needs to be assisted in finding the buckle every.single.time. in every boosterthat has arm rests. This seat and the Maxi Cosi Rodifix are thus winners in this category.

The Flex has a more narrow footprint than others because it doesn't have armrests. Need 3 kids to ride? Need 2 to sit next to one another? You're golden. You can park the Flex next to a variety of seats without issue. I have one next to a Nuna Pipa and a Clek Foonf in a Land Rover Discovery (which doesn't have the broadest back seat).

The Flex adjusts in 4 directions so your picky big kid can decide exactly how the seat is best for them.

As with all Peg Perego products, the fabrics are OUTSTANDING. We have the "licorice" version of the Flex, which is a combo of really soft, highly padded fabrics touching the body and edges with really gorgeous leather finished with white top stitching. This seat isn't more expensive than its competitors, buy it looks and feels like it should be. Super gorgeous, even if you have a luxury car-quality interior.

This seat "makes my buns feel the happiest of any car seat I've ever had!" per my 7 year old. If that isn't a rousing endorsement, I don't know what is.

The seat belt shoulder clip is well-designed so that the belt easily pulls through and retracts without issue (this was a constant issue with the RodiFix, the Oobr, and, to a lesser extent, the Britax Parkway in both my Honda Odyssey and the Discovery).

The folding mechanism seems like a "so what" feature, but is actually really handy. I've used it a handful of times in only a few weeks as I've found myself suddenly needing cargo room. I just remove and fold up the Flex, park it on the front floor, and collapse it's 2nd row seat. Super easy and quick. The latch release and install lever is also delightfully straightforward to use.

All in all, there isn't anything to complain about with this seat. Not even the little pull out cup holders. They're not indestructible, but most European-made seats don't even offer an add on option (like the RodiFix). I also don't mind that there's no bottom as I won't ever have to discover some sort of weird goo science experiment at the bottom of one!

Review:
Britax instructions and customer service is AWFUL! Let me say this--I really like this car seat.
PROS:
- super-easy to install with seatbelt
- the click feature when tightening the straps is really helpful (clicks when straps are appropriately tight around baby)
- decent safety rating last time I checked

CONS:
- Britax communication is horrendous--from their "instructions" to their customer service reps
- the clicktight knob that opens the seat (to remove the car seat) won't turn unless you push down on the seat part...but of course, that's not written anywhere letting you know
- have to buy cupholder separately (after spending $300-400 on the car seat?!?!?!?!)
- the cupholder SUCK, SUCK, SUCKS (very difficult to install and eventually broke trying to re-install it)
- The tether and anchor strap compartments constantly pop open
- if you try to take this on an airplane, it's very heavy. But it doesn't work with Britax's wheeled car seat cart made for that exact purpose.

If you ever have to get in touch with Britax, brace yourself. When I called, I got an incredibly unhelpful, unfriendly customer rep named Brenda, who basically informed me that I've been using it improperly ever since we purchased it! I was calling to ask Britax to explain the bubble diagram on the sides of the seat because, ya know, kinda important to have it installed properly. I found their description of their recline positions to be somewhat confusing. The manual says lighter blue is infant, darker blue is toddler. In another place, it describes the blue for "larger children with head and neck control." In the third place, it says it's important that the seat be reclined to maintain proper head and neck control with "smaller infants." Then a new guideline popped up when their oh-so-friendly phone rep Brenda tells me the bubble should be in the light blue section if the child is under 2 years. I asked sweetheart Brenda if that was written anywhere and she said no. I told her that's a pretty crucial piece of information to not have written anywhere (using my best polite words as opposed WTF ARE YOU GUYS THINKING?!?!) and asked her to pass that along as customer input. She said she would but it seemed that she couldn't care less. Awesome. Since there are NO WORDS on the recline diagram sticker ON the actual car seat describing infant/toddler/age/weight limits, I assumed from the pictures in the bubble area that a younger baby should be reclined further back, but since the standing baby picture is in the darker blue rear-facing and forward-facing, I thought okay, maybe once the baby is 1 year or 20 lbs or maybe standing, you can have it up higher in the dark blue? Apparently, wrong! WTF, Britax?! This is SO important, how could you not have that in writing--like, BOLD writing, too?? It's mind-boggling.

Then I asked lovely Brenda about the cup holder (that I'm sure we all love having to buy separately with such an expensive seat). I ordered it on amazon, but again, their "instructions" have no words, save a few "cautions." Trying to explain the difficulty verbally without being able to show Britax/Brenda was nearly impossible. You can see from the pictures that the opening on the cupholder clip where you slide the holder down onto the car seat appears to be about half as long as it needs to be, as I see it. She kept telling me to just push/shove it down through the crack/gap where the seatbelt would go, and it would "click" in. It never did, and when I push it down, it pulls the gray plastic section of the car seat away, bending it. That seems like a terrible design if that's how it's supposed to attach, or terrible instructions if it's not. I finally got it clicked in, just to find that when I went to close my car door, it hit the cup holder and wouldn't close. This doesn't happen with car seats w/ built-in cup holders (as this seat should absolutely have for the price). So I had to detach it and struggle all over again to put it on the other side of car seat. The rubber piece on the cup holder would hold cups/bottles so tightly that I finally had to take it off so my kiddo could actually get her cup out. Of course, to do this, you have to take the cup holder off again. There isn't a cup/liner within the cupholder that's easily removable, like if drinks spill or the holder gets dirty, so if you ever want to clean it, you have to remove it again. Then struggle to put it back on. It's SUCH a pain in the #*@, I can't truly convey it. I just tried putting it back on yesterday, and after several minutes trying to remember how I'd done it, which I thought was just really jamming it down, as Brenda instructed, it broke. I'm going to call Britax about replacing it... and hope to get someone who's not Brenda.

Another little tidbit they don't tell you is when you push down the cover and it "clicks," securing the seat, when you want to open it, you can't just turn the dial--I wasted a lot of sweat and cussing struggling with that until I realized you need to push down on the cover, then the dial turns pretty easily. I've read other users who've found the same thing. If this is just how it works, why doesn't Britax TELL US THAT?? Seriously, this company needs a friggin' seminar on COMMUNICATION!

Also, as I mentioned above, if you try to take this on an airplane, it's very heavy. You'll want to buy the Britax wheeled cart to go with it... except wait, don't. Because even though that cart is made BY BRITAX, FOR THEIR SEATS, these Clicktights don't have the normal, newer anchor strap connections, so you cannot tighten it onto the cart, meaning not only can your kid not sit in it as you wheel it through the airport, but the seat itself slides off at every turn because it can't be tightened on. My husband and I spent so much time in the airport parking lot trying to figure out how the hell to attach the car seat to the cart that we ended up missing the cutoff for our flight by four minutes. It was a nightmare.

This is the most CAPS-filled review I've ever written. SO ANNOYED with Britax right now. SO annoyed.

Review:

This seat is as heavy as any other convertible seat, there's no advantage in that regard, but my daughter seems to really like the attached cup holders and side pockets for her toys.

The only other thing, is that I found the buckle a little hard to disengage. I have rheumatoid arthritis which has hindered my dexterity, so it has taken me a while to figure out an easy way to disengage the buckle. Because of the way the seat is designed, I definitely suggest that the seat is checked by someone certified to ensure that the height is correct and that the crotch buckle is in the proper position since it can be modified. I also appreciate that the potty training seat covers fit very well in this seat, regardless of brand. Overall, it's a really beautiful seat and I'm glad that I purchased it.
